scenario.description:
# Break Escape SAFETYNET Mission 4: Critical Failure
Virtual machines for the Break Escape SAFETYNET mission 4 narrative experience. These VMs represent the OT-side network at Albion Energy Storage, which ENTROPY's Critical Mass cell reached through a fake maintenance contract (OptiGrid Solutions) and used to falsify the BMS/SCADA thermal telemetry.
## Included Systems
**bms_jump_server** - Debian 12 system sitting between the corporate LAN and the BMS/SCADA segment - Exposed web service carrying the falsified rack status page - ProFTPD service holding OptiGrid's transferred operational intelligence - Erlang/OTP SSH daemon (CVE-2025-32433) left behind by the "maintenance" crew — unauthenticated pre-auth remote code execution - sudoedit (CVE-2023-22809) for local privilege escalation
**kali** - Kali Linux platform for reconnaissance and exploitation against the jump server
## Integration with Break Escape
Provisioned by the Break Escape engine via SecGen integration. The player reaches this network from the engineering workshop terminal and submits recovered flags at the SAFETYNET drop-site terminal in the same room.
IMPORTANT — flag ordering. `Mission#flags_by_vm` (app/models/break_escape/mission.rb:129-139) keys flags by `system_name` and takes them in document order from the generated flag_hints.xml. scenario.json.erb therefore expects exactly four flags on `bms_jump_server`, in this declared order:
flag_1 parameterised_website -> submit_network_scan_flag flag_2 proftpd_133c_backdoor -> submit_ftp_intel_flag flag_3 sudoedit -> submit_privesc_flag flag_4 ssh_erlangotp_rce -> submit_erlang_rce_flag
If a SecGen build emits a different order or count, update `targetFlags` in scenario.json.erb to match — do not renumber here.
## CyBOK Coverage
- Network Security: scanning, service enumeration - Systems Security: vulnerability exploitation, privilege escalation - Cyber-Physical Systems: SCADA/ICS exposure via an OT jump host

OPTIGRID SOLUTIONS -- SITE TRANSFER CHANNEL Cross-cell coordination intel (Critical Mass)
Contract cover: "preventive maintenance, battery management system". Albion believes OptiGrid is a telemetry-calibration vendor. In reality this jump host is ours: it sits between Albion's corporate LAN and the BMS/SCADA segment, and everything the control room trusts passes through it.
Coordination across the cells runs on this channel: - The telemetry stays falsified while the control room trusts the feed. Keep every reading NOMINAL; the operators act on the screen, not on the rack. - The physical work -- the charge-ceiling change on the banks -- is staged under the calibration override, root only. - Hold until the signal. All cells move on the same window.
Operator procedures are not kept here. See the toolkit notes.

BMS CALIBRATION OVERRIDE -- RESTRICTED (root) Albion Energy Storage -- rack banks A / B / C
This override replaces the safe charge ceiling on every bank with the "calibration" profile OptiGrid supplied. The racks are driven past the manufacturer limit while the historian still publishes NOMINAL to the control-room screens.
- Charge ceiling: OVERRIDDEN on Bank A, Bank B and Bank C. - Hydrogen detection and thermal interlocks: reported ARMED, suppressed in the feed. - Emergency shutdown is the only thing left that answers the real state of the racks.
Read at root, this is the whole trick: the plant is being pushed towards thermal runaway while every screen in the control room says it is fine.

OPTIGRID TOOLKIT -- OPERATOR NOTES Maintenance crew, internal use only
This jump server is the way onto Albion's control stack. We left the control-stack service daemon reachable on its high port so the crew can get back in without ever touching Albion's help desk.
- From here, the transfer channel carries the coordination notes. - As root, the calibration override does the real work on the banks. - The falsified rack-status page is what the control room sees. Keep it green. - When the window comes, the override goes live on all three banks at once.
Leave nothing signed. OptiGrid is a shell -- there is no help desk to call.
